title: A Lipschitz map ℝ^m → ℝ^P agrees with countably many C¹ maps off a set with H^m-null image (given scalar C¹ approximation)
statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, and let F : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be K-Lipschitz (ℝ^k = Euclid k). Assume:
(H) for every Lipschitz u : ℝ^m → ℝ (with any constant L ≥ 0) and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is g : ℝ^m → ℝ of class C¹ with L^m({y : u(y) ≠ g(y)}) < ε, where L^m = volume on ℝ^m.
(H) is verbatim the frozen type of the C¹-approximation node c1_approx (Lean dor_lmbsf_lipschitz_c1_approx; Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, value part) at dimension m.
Then there are E ⊆ ℝ^P with H^m(E) = 0 (H^m = μHE[m]) and C¹ maps G_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^P (i ∈ ℕ) such that F(ℝ^m) ⊆ E ∪ ⋃_i G_i(ℝ^m).
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (F : Euclid m → Euclid P) (K : NNReal), LipschitzWith K F → (∀ (u : Euclid m → ℝ) (L : NNReal), LipschitzWith L u → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Euclid m → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {y | u y ≠ g y} < ε) → ∃ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (G : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid P), μHE[m] E = 0 ∧ (∀ i, ContDiff ℝ 1 (G i)) ∧ Set.range F ⊆ E ∪ ⋃ i, Set.range (G i)
